gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-new-: Marker-bold and open-curved, Red Hat Display draws every stroke like a single cable. Noto Sans New Tai Lue sits beneath it with cupped, rounded letters and a lighter touch, so the two share the page without crowding.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-nko: Noto Sans NKo reads modern and approachable, its curves open enough to see straight through. Red Hat Display above it keeps a marker-like line with no pinching at the bends, which gives the heading real punch over the quieter text.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-nko-: Noto Sans NKo Unjoined reads friendly, with wide openings on its small letters. Red Hat Display is cut from one gauge of tubing, and that bold, uniform line against the lighter body is the strongest thing here.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-old-: Noto Sans Old South Arabian reads clean and approachable, its curved strokes stopping before they turn inward. Red Hat Display earns its keep big and short, where its single-thread line can be followed at a glance.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-shav: Red Hat Display cuts every stroke as if with a fixed-width router bit, bold and contemporary with daylight inside each curve. Noto Sans Shavian runs loose and unknotted beneath, so paragraphs feel light.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-znamenny-: Red Hat Display draws tubelike, constant-weight lines that make a bold, contemporary statement at the top of the page. Noto Znamenny Musical Notation keeps its terminals far from the stem, which suits quieter text.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-ojuju: Red Hat Display's lines hold one width, like outlines drawn with a marker. Ojuju follows with the faintest wedge of pen pressure in each curve, so a long stretch of text feels warm and easygoing.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-overpass: Overpass keeps its strokes consistent within every word, and its e shapes never clog into a blot. Red Hat Display handles the loud, marker-bold statements, while the body font handles steady reading.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-palanquin: Red Hat Display holds its thickness steady around every curve, giving headings a bold, contemporary marker line. Palanquin does the quieter work of text, its curved letters keeping wide, unclosed mouths.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-philosopher: Philosopher reads soft and tidy, with curves full of daylight and gentle shifts in thickness. Shrink Red Hat Display, though, or enlarge the body, and the heading's marker-like uniform line loses its authority over the finer text.
